sources.scope: Government of India (MoPNG) clarification via PIB: vehicles from as far back as 2009 have been E20 compatible with respect to fuel system material compatibility. sources.supportingText: Government fleet clarification, not OEM vehicle-specific certification. Applies to manufacturers that designed E20 material compatibility into vehicles from 2009 onwards. sources.scope: PIB PRID 2155558: Government clarification on E20 fleet compatibility. States: 'For some manufacturers, vehicles have been E 20 compatible from as far back as 2009.' Addresses rubber parts and gaskets: 'Only in case of certain older vehicles, some rubber parts and gaskets may require replacement earlier than in case of non blended fuel used. This replacement is inexpensive and can be easily managed during routine servicing. It may need to be done once in the life time of vehicle and is a simple process.' No drivability, startability, metal or plastic compatibility issues under BIS specifications.

sources.scope: Official PIB press release providing government clarification on E20 fuel program. Key statements: (1) 'For some manufacturers, vehicles have been E 20 compatible from as far back as 2009.' (2) 'Only in case of certain older vehicles, some rubber parts and gaskets may require replacement earlier than in case non blended fuel was used. sources.scope: PIB PRID 2155558: Government clarification on E20 fleet compatibility. States: 'For some manufacturers, vehicles have been E 20 compatible from as far back as 2009.' Addresses rubber parts and gaskets: 'Only in case of certain older vehicles, some rubber parts and gaskets may require replacement earlier than in case of non blended fuel used. This replacement is inexpensive and can be easily managed during routine servicing. It may need to be done once in the life time of vehicle and is a simple process.' No drivability, startability, metal or plastic compatibility issues under BIS specifications.

sources.issuer: Pragativadi reporting a Mercedes-Benz India statement
sources.scope: Official Mercedes-Benz India statement (reported by multiple news outlets, July 2026): 'All Mercedes-Benz petrol BS VI vehicles are materially compatible with E20 fuel and certified accordingly by relevant authorities.' Issued in response to YouTuber Sourav Joshi's viral claim that E20 fuel caused significant mileage drop in his Mercedes GLC. Mercedes-Benz India emphasised customer safety, vehicle reliability, and performance, asserting E20 certification by relevant authorities. MD & CEO Santosh Iyer in earlier interviews (Autocar Professional) stated: 'We made every car E20-compatible when we shifted to Euro 6 in 2018, two years ahead of the industry deadline' and noted that from 2024, the company began issuing E20 compliance certificates for all models after ARAI testing.
sources.supportingText: Statement is broad and not model-specific. Claims all BS VI petrol vehicles are E20-compatible, but contradicted by (a) existing owner manuals recommending E10 only, (b) fuel filler caps showing E5/E10, (c) evidence that E20 engineering timeline began April 2023 (three years after BS VI shift). W206 India launch (2022) predates explicit E20 engineering milestone. Statement appears responsive to viral controversy rather than reflecting documented technical specifications. No detailed E20 certification registry by model or production batch published.
sources.title: Mercedes-Benz India Clarifies E20 Fuel Compatibility After Sourav Joshi's Mileage Concerns — Official Advisory, July 2026

Key statements: (1) 'For some manufacturers, vehicles have been E 20 compatible from as far back as 2009.' (2) 'Only in case of certain older vehicles, some rubber parts and gaskets may require replacement earlier than in case non blended fuel was used. This replacement is inexpensive and can be easily managed during routine servicing. It may need to be done once in the life time of vehicle and is a simple process.' (3) 'No issues in drivability, startability, metal compatibility, plastic compatibility' under BIS specifications and Automotive Industry Standards. This release forms the basis for older-vehicle E20 fleet clarification as documented in ROUND2-OLDER-CARS-POLICY.md (2026-07-23).
sources.supportingText: Government policy applies to E20 fuel compatibility nationwide. Individual vehicle E20 certification depends on manufacturer fuel system design and material certification. Rubber parts/gaskets note applies to certain older vehicles—texture represents honest acknowledgment of potential wear items.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (Government of India)
sources.scope: PIB PRID 2155558: Government clarification on E20 fleet compatibility. States: 'For some manufacturers, vehicles have been E 20 compatible from as far back as 2009.' Addresses rubber parts and gaskets: 'Only in case of certain older vehicles, some rubber parts and gaskets may require replacement earlier than in case of non blended fuel used. This replacement is inexpensive and can be easily managed during routine servicing. It may need to be done once in the life time of vehicle and is a simple process.' Confirms no issues in drivability, startability, metal or plastic compatibility under BIS specifications and Automotive Industry Standards.
sources.supportingText: Government policy clarification applies uniformly to eligible vehicle fleet; not model-specific. Establishes material compatibility baseline for vehicles manufactured from 2009 onwards. Applies to Innova Crysta (2016 onwards) cohort as fleet-wide guidance. Seals/gaskets maintenance note is explicit and rides on this record per ROUND2 policy.
sources.title: MoPNG Clarification: E20 Vehicles Compatible from 2009 — Material, Warranty, and Parts Replacement

sources.scope: SIAM statement (30 August 2025): 'SIAM has categorically confirmed warranties will be honoured for vehicles running spec-compliant E20. Whatever warranty is committed by OEMs will be fully honoured for E20 usage.' Cross-referenced with MoPNG Q&A (PRID 2283118): 'virtually every manufacturer today is honoring warranty for all vehicles (old or new)' and ARAI-FIPI-SIAM joint statement (30 Aug 2025): 'Allegations that E20 affects insurance and warranty are baseless.' Applies uniformly across all manufacturers and vehicle ages.
sources.supportingText: Industry-body statement, not OEM-specific. Applies to all vehicles and manufacturers committing warranties under SIAM umbrella. Toyota Innova Crysta (both pre-2020 and 2020+ cohorts) falls under this uniform warranty assurance. No Toyota-specific E20 warranty exclusion or policy published; SIAM industry statement represents the operative warranty framework.
sources.title: SIAM Statement on E20 Warranties and Insurance — Honoured Uniformly Across Manufacturers

sources.issuer: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (Government of India)
sources.scope: PIB PRID 2155558: Government clarification on E20 fleet compatibility. States: 'For some manufacturers, vehicles have been E 20 compatible from as far back as 2009.' Addresses rubber parts and gaskets: 'Only in case of certain older vehicles, some rubber parts and gaskets may require replacement earlier than in case of non blended fuel used. This replacement is inexpensive and can be easily managed during routine servicing. It may need to be done once in the life time of vehicle and is a simple process.' No drivability, startability, metal or plastic compatibility issues under BIS specifications.
sources.supportingText: Government policy clarification applies uniformly to eligible fleet; not model-specific. Establishes material compatibility for vehicles from 2009 onwards; applies to Alto 800 (2012-2023) cohort. Seals/gaskets maintenance note is explicit and rides on this record per policy.
sources.title: MoPNG Clarification: E20 Vehicles Compatible from 2009 — Material, Warranty, and Parts Replacement

sources.issuer: Press Information Bureau / Government of India
sources.scope: PIB Backgrounder containing SIAM statement: 'SIAM has categorically confirmed warranties will be honoured for vehicles running spec-compliant E20.' Statement covers older vehicle cohorts and confirms industry-wide warranty treatment for E20-compatible vehicles. Includes Maruti Suzuki data: 2.84 crore vehicles serviced FY 2025-26, over 1.5 crore 3+ years old, no E20-related issues reported.
sources.supportingText: Industry-body statement published via PIB Backgrounder. Direct SIAM URL (siam.in/article/2281287) is inaccessible (404); statement verified against cached copy of PIB Backgrounder PRID 2281287 dated 2026-07-05. Applies to warranty policy across manufacturers honouring E20 material compatibility claims for spec-compliant vehicles.
sources.title: PIB Backgrounder: SIAM Statement on E20 Fuel Compatibility and Warranty Honour (PRID 2281287)
